---
title: "Components of A Quarto Manual"
format: html
---

A manual page is like any other Quarto document, and is designed to
leverage all of Quarto's features, including executable code chunks, 
cross-references, and citations.

Where manual pages extend Quarto is by requiring that each page
in the manual have at least the following components:

1. A clear and concise page description instructing the user on what to do
and what to expect from the page.

2. An initialization code chunk that can register the project's state before following the instructions.

3. Some external artifact that is generated by the instructions on the page that
the Manual can use as a dependency.

4. A computational test for the artifact.

By defining dependencies in code for each page, a Manual does not
need to be run from end-to-end if the user has already completed some of the steps. 

This page provides a simple example.
